Technical & price structure: In plain terms: Riyad Bank trades meaningfully below our weighted central fair value of SAR 26.61 — the gap is what its retained capital is worth. On the dividend it pays today (~42% of earnings) the shares are worth about SAR 23.6; on the value it builds by reinvesting a ~16% return on equity, the excess-return lenses land at SAR 32.2–33.2. It is Saudi Arabia's third-largest bank by assets — a low-rate, low-cost-deposit franchise earning ~16% on equity against a ~10.3% cost of equity, at a sub-30% cost-to-income ratio. The bull case (~SAR 33) is that the mid-teens ROE persists through the SAMA easing cycle; the cautious case (~SAR 21) is that the margin fades and the ROE settles closer to the cost of equity, which is roughly what the market's ~1.2× book already prices in. What moves it near-term is the SAMA/Fed rate path and the quarterly NIM print.

How is the Riyad Bank valuation calculated? — The study triangulates five lenses — a dividend discount model (the primary lens); a full multi-period residual-income build (book value plus the present value of five years of excess return over the cost of equity, with a through-cycle justified-price-to-book cross-check); an FCFE equity DCF; relative multiples; and a through-cycle normalized-earnings floor — then expresses the result as a 50,000-path Monte Carlo probability distribution. Every assumption is visible and editable in the free Excel model.
